a.text: He leaves the bed of withered flowers.
They say it is a sign of a bountiful harvest.
And so some walked in the embrace of night,
Some shared nectar before the bonfire,
And some walked hand in hand,
Lost together where the story diverged.
Shut the lips that sound the horn, he said.
Close the eyes about to witness eternity, he said.
To pick the fruit of pain.
He leaves the bed of withered flowers.
He writes his epitaph into the stirring dust,

steps.name: Gossipy Manservant
steps.text: Does Lady Dupont still shut herself in her room?

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: It's been three days, and she's hardly touched her food. What shall we do?

steps.name: Gossipy Manservant
steps.text: The way I see it, the madam is fretting over nothing.

steps.name: Gossipy Manservant
steps.text: As heir to the Dupont family, Victoria's most noble lineage, she is both elegant and intelligent, and no one could fault her for choosing any of her three suitors.

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: But that's exactly why she's so troubled.

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: The three Rockefeller brothers may look like they come from the same handsome mold, but they each have wildly different personalities and occupations.

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: When a wise scholar, a brave soldier, and a romantic poet all ask for your hand at once, can you even imagine choosing which to spend your life with?

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: Besides, whatever choice she makes is bound to bring great pain to the other two.

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: Why, the very thought!

steps.name: Gossipy Manservant
steps.text: The very thought of the bonuses we'll get when one of those millionaires moves in! Whatever choice she makes, I hope she chooses soon!

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: How could you be so—
Cut!

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: Director Quay?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Stiff as damned statues.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: (Mutters) Well, it's just exposition anyway. Might as well cut the scene and add a few symbolic empty shots later...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: (Mutters) Let's just hope our overzealous producer lady doesn't sweat the small stuff.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: You two take a break while we make some adjustments to the script... Actually, don't bother coming back for shooting.

steps.name: Gossipy Manservant
steps.text: More adjustments? This guy just can't make up his mind.

steps.name: Worried Maid
steps.text: Shh—

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Alright, people, we're not taking a break just yet. So shut up already... shut up!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Yes yes, I know we've been shooting for two months, and everyone's tired, and the plate's far from the city center, and there are no casinos or shopping districts here, and everything at the self-service bar is undrinkable pisswater...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: BUT! For better or worse, this is our last week. Time is precious and so is my film.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The Death of Lady Dupont is the kind of historical tragedy they don't make in Wrankwood these days, exploring Columbia's changing times through the lens of a noblewoman's marriage...

spans.text: is the kind of historical tragedy they don't make in Wrankwood these days, exploring Columbia's changing times through the lens of a noblewoman's marriage...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: So I don't want it looking like some cheap cash-grab when it finally hits theaters!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Let's move on to the next run-through.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The Death of Lady Dupont, balcony, scene three... Melanie and Michael, you're up.

spans.text: , balcony, scene three... Melanie and Michael, you're up.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What's the matter, Miss Rutherford?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: What do you think, boy?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I shouldn't have made a veteran like you wait a whole minute for me to get ready.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Do you think I'm making a big deal out of nothing?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Of course not. Alongside Marianne Blake, you used to be one of the greatest actresses in Wrankwood.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Seniority, status, etiquette... Hate them as much as you like deep down, but you will respect them on my set.

spans.text: Seniority, status, etiquette... Hate them as much as you like deep down, but you

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I'm sorry if I offended you, ma'am.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: So are we ready?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I know it's not easy playing three different characters, but don't mix them up like you did last time. You're playing the SECOND Rockefeller, the soldier.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: You're at Lady Dupont's manor, and have just thrown away your older brother's flowers and torn up your younger brother's love letter. You're rushing into your beloved's bedroom to pour your heart out!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Silence, please—Action!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Believe me, my love, my two brothers could never match my feelings for you!

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I've heard more than enough honeyed words, Mr. Rockefeller.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Were I not the scion of Dupont, were our union to bring the Rockefellers no wealth or status in high society, would you still—

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You wound me. I am no schemer, and I mean every word I say.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You know I'm not as smart or sensitive as my brothers. How can I hope to move you, if not through the sincerity of my feelings?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: And how will you prove it?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I recently returned from the battlefield, where I brushed shoulders with death.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: When that shell burst right next to me, when I felt my body and my senses flying away, when I came close to death's door...

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: All I could picture was your face, your smile!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Er... you have the next line, ma'am—

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Despicable.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Uh—What?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: What kind of soldier would twist his face up like you did when speaking of the battlefield? You put so much honey in your words, you could stick a fly to the ground with it.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I know you've spent the last two months making moves on anything even vaguely female on this plate, but for God's sake keep your private life off the set, boy.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Not everyone will fall for a wiggle of your ears and a swoosh of your orange tail like that dumb blonde.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: D-Dumb blonde...?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: M-Marion! What are you doing here?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Why wouldn't the costume designer be on set for the run-through? I need to see if the costumes are in order.

spans.text: the costume designer be on set for the run-through? I need to see if the costumes are in order.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Or what? Don't tell me you also believe that gossip the rest of the crew's been spreading?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Right, of course. There's no problem.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Moving on... Michael, your performance needs to fit the character better, or it won't come across as sincere.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The second Rockefeller's sincerity is the whole point. Without it, how can we possibly convince the audience that this is what pushes Lady Dupont to finally make her decision?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: You two can take a break while we move on to the next one.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Abner?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: I'm here.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: We need an evocative transition into the next scene.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Gotcha. We'll go with the plan we talked about yesterday.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Also, can you stay away from that metal rack? I'm worried the screws will scratch the camera.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I can't tell if you're the winner of Wrankwood's Best Cinematography award, or the least professional cameraman in town.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Why not both?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: What happened to you, man?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: No need to make a fuss of it.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: As Lady Dupont and the second Rockefeller's conversation fades out, the camera pans away from the balcony...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: It moves down the steps, across a row of portraits and antique vases, to the front hall draped with red curtains.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The front door opens.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The sound of wind and rain trespasses into the quiet manor. The camera follows, and a black shadow enters the frame—

steps.name: Mysterious and Elegant Creature
steps.text: Mrrow~

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: What the hell's that black shadow?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Is it a ghost? A prop? A hallucination? Somebody's Friedkin pet?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Do none of you idiots realize what kind of havoc an animal like this could wreak on a film set?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Grab it, Abner! Don't let it mess with the camera rails on the ground!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: With what hands? Or do you want me to smash the damned camera?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: It went your way, Marion.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: I don't have any free hands either! And are you prepared to take responsibility if the costumes get wrinkled? The producer would have a fit!

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Someone stop it!

steps.name: Mysterious and Elegant Creature
steps.text: Mrow—

The mysterious and elegant creature darts through the set, weaving between the wires and delicate equipment laid out over the ground, its two tails moving this way and that as cries are heard up and down the crowd...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Stop painting that background and catch that thing, Tippi! And you there, the prop intern—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Her name is Moira. Moi-ra.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Forget it, Tippi.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: You're, like, way too nice, Molly. You can't let people walk all over you.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Who cares? Just catch that thing!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I-It stopped.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Well, aren't you a cutie! You're even more mysterious than the monster in that horror flick I saw last night!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Mind if I use you as reference for the street scene?

steps.name: Mysterious and Elegant Creature
steps.text: Meow...
The mysterious and elegant creature settles onto the prop box, looking up at the two girls with what seems to be displeasure.
Moira cannot help but bend down and reach out to it, but as she looks into its clear blue eyes she feels her mind go blank...
The next moment, the creature has vanished from the set.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Finally...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: How could you idiots let it get away from right under your noses?!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Now, now, Marion.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm the one you're mad at. No need to take it out on the newcomers.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: You...
If you're going to argue, take it outside. Or better yet, off the plate.
After all, no one expects professionalism out there.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Greta.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Back to work, people.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I thought you'd be more upset about the shoot being delayed.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I'm not THAT harsh, Steven. Besides, her appearance on set means we're in for a wonderful surprise when it's time to shoot.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'Her'?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Wait, you mean that creature?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Who else?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: She's the companion of a guest of mine... and her showing up means that he's finally made up his mind.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: He'll play the Messenger who appears in the next scene.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Isn't that right...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Lucian?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: ...As you wish.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Miss.Christine is free. None may interfere with her intentions or actions.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I apologize on her behalf.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Hold up, we're making a last minute cast change, just for some pretty boy no one's heard of?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: It's only a minor role. No need to feel threatened, my handsome leading man Michael.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: And it's not out of nowhere. Greta gave me a heads-up earlier.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Fine, fine.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I'm glad you've made your decision, Lucian. Film is a very different beast from stage, so I understand why you needed to take your time thinking it over.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: But that costume fits you so well. I was right to invite you. I guarantee you'll be the next big thing in Wrankwood.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I can only hope.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Well, we've delayed enough. If the actors are ready, let's get on with the run-through.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I take it you've got your lines down, Lucian?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I could recite them backwards.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Alright then... The Death of Lady Dupont, front hall, scene four, action.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: As the second Rockefeller pours his heart out to Lady Dupont on the balcony, a young Messenger from afar pushes open the front door.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: He's welcomed by Lady Dupont's brother, who always seems to have a lot on his mind—

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Oh, for God's sake—where's Sir Dupont?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: —Dalton!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Where the Hitchcock has he run off to this time? Drinking again?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Where's my coordinator? Shelly?
We're here, we're here.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Thank goodness... *pant*... I found him... I brought Dalton!

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: (Drunken eyes)

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: (Hiccups)

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I realized he was missing when I took a head count at the waiting area.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I searched every food cart, self-service bar, and outdoor rest area—anywhere that might have booze... I finally found him in some bushes by the road.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Knife... I found the *hic* knife!

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: He said he was looking for the knife prop that the Messenger is supposed to 'kill' Sir Dupont with.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: So which one of you sent a drunk to go hunt down a prop? Where's the prop master, Moira?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I-I don't know...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Fine, whatever, as long as we've got the prop.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Costume crew! Get his clothes in order!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: You do remember what you're playing in this scene, right?

spans.text: remember what you're playing in this scene, right?

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Of course... a corpse. Nobody does it better. Haha.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Pathetic.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: *hic* What'd ya say?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I simply can't stand people like you.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: You used to be the darling of Wrankwood when pioneer films were in their heyday. Producers were queuing up to book you.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: And now you're just going to let yourself rot, like mud in a pit?

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Wh-What do you know?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I couldn't care less what you've been through. But at least show a shred of self-respect in front of the younger generation.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: ...That's one of the rules of Wrankwood, too.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: You're playing opposite a man who's standing in front of a camera for the first time.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Fine, fine.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: *hic*—Whasyourname?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Lucian. You may also call me... Phantom.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Whatever.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Sorry kid, didn't know this was your first shoot. But don't worry, just follow my lead. I can play this role hammered, no problem.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: I'm gonna *hic* try to kill ya to shut ya up, 'cause of the news you brought...

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: We get to scuffling, then you grab this knife and stab me with it... It's a prop so the blade just slides into the handle. I got a blood bag in my chest pocket, and it'll pop with just a little pressure.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Just don't get stuck on thinking 'when am I gonna grab the knife', or you won't get in character. Got it?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You've read through that letter three times now, Sir Dupont.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: If there's no issue with it, please assemble everyone in the household so I can read it to them.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Huh?
Dalton's eyes meet the young man's, and he swallows the drunken hiccup that had reached the front of his throat.
He sees not a rookie actor on a film set for the first time, but a Messenger who had come all the way from Victoria, his gaze tired but strong.
The studio falls silent. Director Quay has yet to call 'action', but Dalton can feel his counterpart's focus, and Abner's camera points towards them—
He is looking at a natural.
And so he takes a deep breath—

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: No, this is an official letter from Victoria's royal house. I can't let you read it aloud.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: If people were to hear that the Dupont bloodline is all a lie, then my sister's marriage to any of the Rockefellers will be called off!

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: All that wealth, all that money that should have been mine, my very future... All gone in an instant, like popping a balloon.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Can't you just leave, boy? Pretend you were never here... I'll give you money. I'll give you all the money you want!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You have no authority over me.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: You're just a Messenger! What part of this has anything to do with you?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The truth.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: True, what happens to this household has nothing to do with me. But I've got something to do with the truth, sir.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Even if I turned around and left right now, the truth of the Dupont family will still have kicked open your door, forevermore.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I have no power to take away your misfortune. All I can do is to announce its coming—whether you're willing to face it or not.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: For such is my wretched fate!
Dalton looks into the young man's eyes and sees the deep pain and sorrow within.
Suddenly, he feels like he has never been so sober.
He does not need to recall his lines. They come to him naturally.
'Pain? Sorrow?'
'Laughable!'
'Who do you think you are?'
Dalton pulls his knife and swings it at the young man—
Sir Dupont and the young Messenger fight over the deadly weapon. It takes only a moment for it to change hands, their actions as coordinated as if they had rehearsed it a thousand times.

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Pain?

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Sorrow?

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Laughable! Who do you think you are?

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: I will not let you ruin what should be mine!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: As I said, sir, my only connection here is to the truth.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: From the noble halls of Victoria, to the ruins of Gaul, to the Basilica of Laterano, to the coastline of Iberia...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I've walked all four corners of Terra, delivering the silent message of death, and bearing witness to countless meaningless tragedies. The story of the Duponts is but one of them.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: And while I have never sought it, the truth always reveals itself before my eyes—

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Such is my wretched fate!

steps.name: Dalton
steps.text: Shut up!
Sir Dupont desperately lunges at the young man before him. The face of the Messenger has become twisted in the struggle.
He notices the young man pause for an instant, then grip the knife again. The point of the knife approaches his chest—
This man must have felt the weight of fate, he thinks.
A lifeless body falls to the ground. Blood, rose petals, the wind and rain.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Cut!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Did you get all that, Abner? I think we might be able to use this take as is!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Sure did!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: (Claps)

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Is this really this guy's first time on camera, Steven?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Greta said he used to be part of a theater troupe.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Oh, a stage actor...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Honestly, I'm more shocked by Dalton. I haven't seen such a convincing performance from him in ages.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Get up, Dalton! We're packing up. But if you want a drink tonight, I'm buying! Haha—

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: ...Dalton?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Why isn't he getting up? Check on him, Shelly!
It is as if the air has frozen.
Dalton lies in front of the steps, not stirring even as Shelly dashes to his side.
The blood bag in his suit pocket has already run dry, but blood continues to seep from his chest.
Filled with a terrifying thought, Shelly reaches out toward the red liquid on the ground with a trembling hand—
It is warm, sticky, and metallic.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Th-This is real blood!
